# mfcuk

**MIFARE Classic key recovery with no known key — the slow path**

- **Version recorded:** 0.3.8
- **Categories:** `rfid`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/nfc-tools/mfcuk>

## What it does

Implements the 'darkside' attack, recovering a first sector key from a MIFARE Classic card without needing any key to begin with.

## Why you would want it

It is what you use when mfoc cannot start because every default key has been changed. In practice the pair are used together: mfcuk to recover one key, mfoc to expand that into the rest.

## Before it will work

A libnfc-supported reader and patience -- this attack takes minutes to hours where mfoc takes seconds.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`rfid`](../profiles/rfid.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install mfcuk --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `mfcuk`

## Known problems

Much slower and much less reliable than mfoc, and it does not work against every card revision. Upstream has been quiet since 2018. Both tools predate the hardened MIFARE Classic EV1 variants, against which neither works.
